scenes.tts: How does a neuron keep its own branches from tangling, while still overlapping its neighbours?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Badge Only You Wear. One white dendritic arbor; a second arbor in another colour overlaps it.
scenes.narration: How does a neuron keep its own branches from tangling, while still overlapping its neighbours?

scenes.tts: Take one neuron's arbor. Its branches often spread evenly, without crossing or bundling.
scenes.visual: The white branches fill the territory evenly; none cross.
scenes.narration: Take one neuron's arbor. Its branches often spread evenly, without crossing or bundling.

scenes.tts: This is self-avoidance. Sister branches from the same cell touch, then move apart.
scenes.visual: A branch tip touches a sister branch and retracts. Label: self-avoidance.
scenes.narration: This is self-avoidance. Sister branches from the same cell touch, then move apart.

scenes.tts: Yet fly sensory neurons share the body wall with other classes, and their dendrites overlap.
scenes.visual: Fly body wall: two classes of sensory neuron, in two colours, overlapping on the same patch.
scenes.narration: Yet fly sensory neurons share the body wall with other classes, and their dendrites overlap.

scenes.tts: At every contact, a branch must ask: is this me, or someone else?
scenes.visual: Two branch tips touch; a question mark: me, or someone else?
scenes.narration: At every contact, a branch must ask: is this me, or someone else?

scenes.tts: Predict. A protein binds only identical copies, and binding makes branches pull apart. What must it be like?
scenes.visual: On screen: Predict. What must the protein be like?
scenes.narration: Predict. A protein binds only identical copies, and binding makes branches pull apart. What must it be like?

scenes.tts: Every branch of one neuron must carry the same version, so sister branches always match.
scenes.visual: All white branches carry the same badge colour.
scenes.narration: Every branch of one neuron must carry the same version, so sister branches always match.

scenes.tts: Neighbouring neurons must carry different versions, so their branches seldom match.
scenes.visual: The blue neuron's branches carry a different badge.
scenes.narration: Neighbouring neurons must carry different versions, so their branches seldom match.

scenes.tts: The fly has such a protein, from one gene, Dee-scam one. It comes in many isoforms.
scenes.caption: The fly has such a protein, from one gene, Dscam1. It comes in many isoforms.
scenes.visual: Gene label: Dscam1, Drosophila. Credit: Schmucker, Zipursky and colleagues, 2000. Definition: isoforms, forms of one protein made from one gene.
scenes.narration: The fly has such a protein, from one gene, Dscam1. It comes in many isoforms.

scenes.tts: Exons are the stretches of a gene kept in its messenger RNA. Four of Dee-scam one's exons come as clusters of alternatives.
scenes.visual: Four exon clusters drawn as boxes of 12, 48, 33 and 2. Definition: exon, a stretch of a gene kept in the messenger RNA.
scenes.narration: Exons are the stretches of a gene kept in its messenger RNA. Four of Dscam1's exons come as clusters of alternatives.
scenes.caption: Exons are the stretches of a gene kept in its messenger RNA. Four of Dscam1's exons come as clusters of alternatives.

scenes.tts: Each messenger RNA keeps one exon from each cluster.
scenes.visual: One exon is picked from each of the four boxes.
scenes.narration: Each messenger RNA keeps one exon from each cluster.

scenes.tts: That gives nineteen thousand and eight outer surfaces, and thirty-eight thousand and sixteen isoforms in all.
scenes.caption: That gives 19,008 outer surfaces, and 38,016 isoforms in all.
scenes.visual: On screen only: 12 × 48 × 33 = 19,008 outer domains; × 2 = 38,016 isoforms. The counter multiplies up.
scenes.narration: That gives 19,008 outer surfaces, and 38,016 isoforms in all.

scenes.tts: The fourth cluster builds the stretch that crosses the membrane, so it does not change the outer surface.
scenes.visual: The cluster of 2 highlighted inside the membrane; the outer domains above it unchanged.
scenes.narration: The fourth cluster builds the stretch that crosses the membrane, so it does not change the outer surface.

scenes.tts: Each isoform binds mainly to identical isoforms. But matched branches pull apart. Same means retreat.
scenes.visual: Two identical isoforms bind face to face; mismatched pairs do not. Credit: Wojtowicz, Zipursky and colleagues, 2004. Then two matching branches spring apart. Word on screen: retreat.
scenes.narration: Each isoform binds mainly to identical isoforms. But matched branches pull apart. Same means retreat.

scenes.tts: Remove Dee-scam one, and a neuron's own branches cross and bundle.
scenes.caption: Remove Dscam1, and a neuron's own branches cross and bundle.
scenes.visual: Genotype table, row 2: no Dscam1. The white arbor's branches cross and clump. Credit: three groups, 2007.
scenes.narration: Remove Dscam1, and a neuron's own branches cross and bundle.

scenes.tts: Take a neuron that lacks Dee-scam one and give it a single isoform, and its own branches spread apart again.
scenes.visual: Row 3: one neuron lacking Dscam1, given back a single isoform, neighbours normal. Own branches spread apart; overlap with neighbours kept.
scenes.narration: Take a neuron that lacks Dscam1 and give it a single isoform, and its own branches spread apart again.
scenes.caption: Take a neuron that lacks Dscam1 and give it a single isoform, and its own branches spread apart again.

scenes.tts: Predict. Now give every neuron the same single isoform. What happens between neighbours?
scenes.visual: Row 4 appears with a blank cell. On screen: Predict.
scenes.narration: Predict. Now give every neuron the same single isoform. What happens between neighbours?

scenes.tts: Neighbours that carry the same single isoform cannot tell themselves from each other. The logic predicts they avoid each other.
scenes.visual: The blank fills, labelled predicted: neighbours avoid each other. The blue and white arbors pull apart.
scenes.narration: Neighbours that carry the same single isoform cannot tell themselves from each other. The logic predicts they avoid each other.

scenes.tts: Flies whose Dee-scam one could make only one outer surface had severely disorganised circuits.
scenes.caption: Flies whose Dscam1 could make only one outer surface had severely disorganised circuits.
scenes.visual: Credit: Hattori, Demir and colleagues, 2007. A tangled circuit schematic.
scenes.narration: Flies whose Dscam1 could make only one outer surface had severely disorganised circuits.

scenes.tts: Which isoform a neuron carries matters little. Differing from its neighbours is what matters.
scenes.visual: Card: which isoform matters little; being different matters.
scenes.narration: Which isoform a neuron carries matters little. Differing from its neighbours is what matters.

scenes.tts: Why thousands? Picture each neuron drawing about twenty badges from a bowl.
scenes.visual: A neuron draws about 20 badges from a bowl. Illustrative model, not a measured count.
scenes.narration: Why thousands? Picture each neuron drawing about twenty badges from a bowl.

scenes.tts: From a small bowl, a neighbour carries many of your badges.
scenes.visual: Bowl of 48: about 40% of your badges also on a neighbour. Numbers on screen only.
scenes.narration: From a small bowl, a neighbour carries many of your badges.

scenes.tts: From a huge bowl, a neighbour carries almost none.
scenes.visual: Bowl of 19,008: about 0.1% shared. Numbers on screen only.
scenes.narration: From a huge bowl, a neighbour carries almost none.

scenes.tts: In the huge bowl, sister branches match completely and a neighbour only slightly. Flies need thousands of isoforms to wire normally.
scenes.visual: Two bars: sister branches, full match; neighbour, a sliver. Credit: Hattori and colleagues, 2009: thousands needed.
scenes.narration: In the huge bowl, sister branches match completely and a neighbour only slightly. Flies need thousands of isoforms to wire normally.

scenes.tts: Mouse Dee-scam is not spliced this way.
scenes.caption: Mouse DSCAM is not spliced this way.
scenes.visual: Mouse retina. A starburst amacrine cell with many overlapping neighbours of its own type.
scenes.narration: Mouse DSCAM is not spliced this way.

scenes.tts: Instead, starburst amacrine cells use gamma protocadherins, adhesion proteins of the cadherin family. Without them, each cell's own dendrites cross and clump.
scenes.visual: Credit: Lefebvre, Sanes and colleagues, 2012. Label: protocadherins, cadherin-family adhesion proteins. Knockout starburst cell with crossing dendrites.
scenes.narration: Instead, starburst amacrine cells use gamma protocadherins, adhesion proteins of the cadherin family. Without them, each cell's own dendrites cross and clump.

scenes.tts: In starburst cells lacking the protocadherins, give every cell the same single isoform. Each arbor separates, but neighbours avoid each other too.
scenes.visual: Protocadherin-deficient starburst cells, all in one colour; each arbor is tidy, but neighbouring arbors pull apart.
scenes.narration: In starburst cells lacking the protocadherins, give every cell the same single isoform. Each arbor separates, but neighbours avoid each other too.

scenes.tts: With only about fifty-eight genes, recognition is thought to compare the whole combination, not single isoforms.
scenes.caption: With only about 58 genes, recognition is thought to compare the whole combination, not single isoforms.
scenes.visual: A cell's set of protocadherins shown as a row of badges; in the proposed model, the whole row is compared. Label: current model.
scenes.narration: With only about 58 genes, recognition is thought to compare the whole combination, not single isoforms.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: a label unique to one cell, read as retreat, keeps that cell's own branches apart.
scenes.visual: Closing card: unique label, read as retreat, keeps your own branches apart.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: a label unique to one cell, read as retreat, keeps that cell's own branches apart.
